title: Server chips aren't tied to sessions, and a page <title> replaces even the repo name: 'Directory listing for /', two identical 'Vite + React + TS' chips from two repos
repro: Open Home (one click on Net)
In beacon's repo run `python3 -m http.server 47102`
Or ask the vibepet session to run `python3 -m http.server 47120 --bind 127.0.0.1` in the background (Bash run_in_background)
Or run two servers titled 'Vite + React + TS' from kestrel's repo (:47153) and beacon's repo (:47154)
Wait ≤15 s for the localhost chips
expected: Each chip names the session that runs it (or at least its repo), e.g. ':47120 vibepet · Directory listing', and that session's row shows its servers, so with 10 sessions I can tell whose server is whose.
actual: Chips read ':47102 Directory listing for /', ':47120 Directory listing for /', ':47153 Vite + React + TS' and ':47154 Vite + React + TS': no session and no repo. The vibepet session's own server (process chain Python ← bash ← that session's claude) is not linked to the 'Read package.json · vibepet' row. The repo appears only one level deep in the native ⋯ → Localhost submenu ('http.server (vibepet) — ~/.vibepet-ultra/fleet/vibepet'). Cause: the renderer label is `s.title || ports.label(s)` and nothing maps a server to a session (no pid ancestry, cwd only, and that never reaches the chip).
member: vibepet (its own background server), beacon, kestrel
truth: vibepet done (registry idle, last end_turn) with its Bash background server running as its child; beacon question (waiting(input needed)); kestrel approval (waiting(permission prompt))

title: Title probe and Open assume http://127.0.0.1 / http://localhost: a [::1]-only server (Node listen('localhost'), Vite's default) gets Open disabled and no title; two servers on one port share one title and one target; HTTPS servers can't be opened
repro: Open Home
In the vibepet repo run a node server with `listen(47181, 'localhost')`: it binds [::1] only on this Mac, like Vite's default host. Titled 'Vite + React + TS'
Wait for its chip
Separately: kestrel node server on *:47151 ('Kestrel dashboard') and beacon `python3 -m http.server 47151 --bind 127.0.0.1` ('Beacon status'). Click Open on each chip
Separately: an HTTPS dev server on 127.0.0.1:47183
expected: The probe and Open use the address and scheme each listener is bound to: the [::1] server shows its title with Open working; each of the two :47151 servers shows its own title and opens its own server; the HTTPS one opens https://.
actual: [::1] server: chip ':47181 node (vibepet)' with Open disabled, while http://localhost:47181 answers 200 'Vite + React + TS'; the probe to 127.0.0.1 is refused. Shared port: two identical chips ':47151 Beacon status' (the kestrel one has beacon's title), and Open on either requests http://localhost:47151, which reaches 'Kestrel dashboard' (::1 first), so beacon's server can't be opened. HTTPS: ':47183 node (vibepet)', Open disabled. On this Mac, 14 of the 51 listeners the unisolated filter would show are bound to [::1] only (counts only).
truth: kestrel approval, beacon question, vibepet done; servers verified with lsof: [::1]:47181, *:47151 + 127.0.0.1:47151, 127.0.0.1:47183

title: A dev server still compiling when first seen keeps Open disabled and a generic label for good: one 800 ms probe per pid:port, never retried
repro: Open Home
In the vibepet repo start a server where every request waits until 20 s after start, then is instant: a Next.js first build (fx/slow2.js 47185 'Next.js app' 20000)
Wait for its chip, then 50 s and three more list refreshes
expected: Once the server answers, the chip shows its title and Open works. The probe is retried after a timeout.
actual: First seen 13.0 s after listen as ':47185 node (vibepet)' with Open disabled. 50 s after listen it was unchanged, while http://localhost:47185 returned 200 'Next.js app'. The native menu's 'Open http://localhost:47185' is disabled too (same `http !== false` flag), so the pet offers no way to open it. ports.js caches the first probe's result in `titles` for the life of the pid:port.
truth: vibepet done (idle/end_turn); server listening on *:47185 the whole time

title: New servers show up ~9 s late and dead ones linger ~11 s (the list refreshes every 12 s); the anchor is ≤3 s
repro: Open Home
At a random moment start a server in a session repo (node or `python3 -m http.server`)
Time listen → chip rendered
At a random moment stop it (Ctrl-C), time exit → chip gone
Repeat ×8
expected: A new server shows ≤3 s after it starts listening, and an exited one is gone ≤3 s after it exits (rubric 95 anchor for detection).
actual: Start → chip: median 8.7 s (3.8–15.0 s, n=8 at random moments; pooled median 9.2 s, n=15). Exit → gone: median 11.0 s (4.5–15.4 s, n=8; pooled 10.5 s, n=14). The in-app refresh interval was 12.0 s (11.6–12.4 s, n=33): ports.poll(10e3) only starts a refresh on a 3 s tick ≥10 s after the last, and its result is picked up on the next tick. 1-min load 3.2–10.5 during the trials; no sleep or wake.
truth: kestrel approval, beacon question, vibepet done throughout (fleet status at start and end of both runs)

title: Chips are pid:port pairs while Stop kills a pid: a prefork server becomes 4 chips, Stop on a worker is undone by its master, and Stop on a debugger-port chip names another port and kills both
repro: Open Home
In the vibepet repo start a prefork server (master + 3 workers sharing 127.0.0.1:47184, gunicorn shape)
Click ✕ on a worker's chip, confirm Stop
Separately: `node --inspect=127.0.0.1:47163 app.js` serving :47162; click ✕ on the :47163 chip
expected: One chip per server (port). Stop ends the server: its process group or master, or says it is managed. The dialog names every port that will go down.
actual: Prefork: four identical ':47184 gunicorn app' chips, half of the 8-chip budget. Stop on a worker killed that worker; the master replaced it 20 ms later; the server kept answering and still showed 4 chips. The only message, 'stopped pid 47120', was behind the panel. Debugger: ✕ on ':47163' asked 'Stop node (vibepet) on :47162?' (local-stop looks the pid up and takes its first port), and both :47162 and :47163 died.

repro: Open Home with a server chip listed (vibepet site preview, `python3 -m http.server 47141 --directory site`)

title: At the default alert level every localhost event is dropped: a crashed server vanishes silently, and Stop from the ⋯ → Localhost menu gives no feedback at all
repro: Keep alerts at the default ('+ Finished')
Click ⋯ → Localhost → ':47192 menu target' → 'Stop node (pid 63602)…' and confirm
Separately: let a listed server exit (Ctrl-C)
expected: The result of my own Stop is always reported. A dev server that dies while I'm away is worth one quiet line, e.g. 'kestrel's server on :47101 stopped'.
actual: Menu Stop: the process died in 19 ms, but no event reached the renderer (localMenu's stopIt uses emit('localhost'), which QUIET.done drops), so there is no message of any kind. Only with alerts set to 'Everything' are up/down lines sent, and then they merge unrelated servers ('…:47169 is up · …:47168 went down') and hide behind an open panel.
truth: vibepet done; kestrel approval; beacon question
